# Phase 04.1 — Setup Hardening and Trust Checks

Source of truth: [Proposal 04](../proposals/04-automatic-context-engine.md)  
Build plan reference: [04 build plan](../../.codebuddy/plans/04-automatic-context-engine-build-plan.md)

## Objective

Make `codebuddy use` and local setup feel production-grade for a senior
developer using their own Postgres or the bundled Docker path.

This phase is about trust, onboarding, and safe defaults. It must not drift
into token-savings or automatic memory features yet.

## Build targets

- Make `codebuddy use` the default happy path.
- Add stronger local Postgres diagnostics.
- Add `codebuddy db doctor` and `codebuddy db test` or equivalent subcommands.
- Scaffold `.codebuddy/policies.yaml`.
- Add doctor checks for:
  - missing `.codebuddy` scaffold;
  - unsafe config permissions;
  - missing policy scaffold;
  - unreachable Postgres;
  - mismatched namespace/setup assumptions.
- Improve setup output so the user always knows the next action.

## Must preserve

- Existing `codebuddy use` workflows.
- Existing BYO Postgres flow.
- Existing bundled Docker flow.
- Local-first trust model.
- No secret leakage to logs.

## Non-goals

- No background indexing.
- No automatic memory extraction.
- No LLM-driven setup.
- No new hosted dependency.

## Implementation notes

- Prefer extending existing setup/doctor commands instead of inventing parallel flows.
- Keep config and scaffold logic centralized.
- Make errors actionable, not generic.
- If a setup path degrades, say exactly what still works and what does not.

## Verification checklist

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run lint`
- targeted tests for setup and doctor
- full `npm test` if setup paths or shared config code changes substantially

## Codex / Claude execution prompt

```text
You are a senior software developer working on CodeBuddy Phase 04.1 from
Proposal 04 — Automatic Context Engine.

Your mission:
Implement setup hardening and trust checks only. Follow Proposal 04 exactly.
Do not drift into indexing, token savings, automatic memory capture, or
suggestion-engine work.

What to build in this phase:
- strengthen `codebuddy use`;
- improve local Postgres diagnostics;
- add DB health commands or equivalent;
- scaffold `.codebuddy/policies.yaml`;
- improve `doctor` so setup failures are obvious and actionable.

Engineering standards:
- preserve backward compatibility where practical;
- prefer small coherent edits over broad refactors;
- keep setup logic deterministic and easy to test;
- never log secrets or leak tokens;
- do not introduce hidden hosted services or hidden side effects.

Before editing:
1. Read the existing setup flow, doctor flow, config-file logic, and scaffold logic.
2. Identify the smallest set of files that should change.
3. Check whether current tests already cover the paths you are touching.

While implementing:
- centralize repeated setup checks where that reduces breakage risk;
- keep user messaging explicit and calm;
- ensure BYO Postgres remains first-class;
- preserve local-first storage assumptions.

Testing expectations:
- add or update tests for every changed setup branch that could regress;
- run typecheck, lint, and the smallest relevant test selection first;
- run broader tests if shared setup/config code changes.

Deliverable:
- setup feels easier;
- failures explain themselves;
- doctor catches missing scaffold and database issues clearly.
```

## Completion prompt

```text
Before marking Phase 04.1 complete:
1. Verify the implementation matches Proposal 04 Phase 1 and nothing beyond it.
2. Re-check that no secret values can appear in logs or generated files.
3. Run the relevant verification commands and fix failures instead of deferring them.
4. Summarize what changed, what was verified, and any remaining known gap.

Do not call the phase complete if the happy path works but the degraded/error
paths remain ambiguous or untested.
```
